channel.title: PsyDigest — psychiatry literature digest
channel.description: Summaries of new psychiatric research and guidelines

item.title: Nutraceuticals and phytoceuticals in the treatment of bipolar disorder: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and acceptability of nutraceuticals and phytoceuticals (e.g., vitamins, herbal products) for treating bipolar disorder (BD) in randomized controlled trials (RCTs), addressing a gap in evidence for these adjunctive or alternative treatments.
FINDINGS: Twenty-eight RCTs (n=2,222) assessed 22 treatments. No nutraceutical outperformed placebo for depressive symptoms; placebo outperformed palmitoylethanolamide (SMD=2.69, 95% CI 1.43–3.95) in one trial with high heterogeneity (I²=86%). For manic symptoms, palmitoylethanolamide (SMD=-4.58, 95% CI -6.24 to -2.92) and folic acid (SMD=-2.42, 95% CI -4.06 to -0.79) outperformed placebo, but with substantial heterogeneity (I²=91.3%). Only one RCT supported palmitoylethanolamide’s effect, and meta-regression linked larger effects to lower methodological quality (AMSTAR-Plus scores). Confidence in evidence (CINeMA) was predominantly low or very low.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is weak, with high heterogeneity, reliance on single small trials, and low methodological quality ratings. The statistically significant findings for manic symptoms are not robust due to inconsistency, small sample sizes, and potential bias. No treatment can be recommended based on current data; further high-quality RCTs are urgently needed.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Clinicians should not use nutraceuticals or phytoceuticals as evidence-based treatments for acute bipolar depression or mania. Patients using these products should be monitored closely, and clinicians should discuss the lack of robust evidence supporting their efficacy.

item.title: Pharmacological interventions for alcohol use disorder on quality of life: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 randomized controlled trials (n=4376) examined whether pharmacotherapies for alcohol use disorder (AUD) improve mental and physical quality of life (QoL), a key outcome for sustaining recovery.
FINDINGS: Naltrexone improved both mental QoL (d=0.30, 95% CI 0.08–0.52) and physical QoL (d=0.16, 95% CI 0.01–0.31). Nalmefene improved physical QoL (d=0.13, 95% CI 0.02–0.25) but not mental QoL (d=0.18, 95% CI –0.004 to 0.354). Topiramate showed no clear benefit, though a post-hoc analysis suggested a small physical QoL gain linked to reduced heavy drinking. Evidence for other agents (acamprosate, sertraline, psilocybin) was based on single trials.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is moderate in size but heterogeneous, with small effect sizes and limited data for many drugs. Risk of bias was assessed with Cochrane RoB 2, but selective reporting and heterogeneity limit certainty. Statistically significant effects do not necessarily translate into clinically meaningful improvements in daily functioning or well-being.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current pharmacotherapies may offer modest QoL benefits for some patients with AUD, but routine QoL monitoring is not yet supported by robust evidence. Clinicians should individualize treatment and consider QoL outcomes alongside traditional measures like abstinence or relapse rates.

item.title: Psychosocial interventions for military personnel with PTSD: protocol of a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The review asks which psychosocial interventions are most effective for military personnel with PTSD and how their components compare, using a planned network meta-analysis of existing trials. This matters because PTSD is common in this population and multiple therapies exist but head-to-head evidence is sparse.
FINDINGS: The protocol describes a systematic review followed by network meta-analysis to compare all psychological interventions for PTSD in current and former military personnel. It will also examine which specific treatment components drive benefit when delivered in combination. The team will involve lived-experience advisors, clinicians and researchers throughout.
INTERPRETATION: Because this is a protocol rather than completed analyses, no effect sizes, confidence intervals or p-values are yet available. The planned methods (network meta-analysis) can rank treatments even when they have never been directly compared, but the eventual certainty of the evidence will depend on the number and quality of included studies, their comparators and risk of bias. Involvement of stakeholders is a strength that may improve relevance to practice.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: At present, this protocol signals that updated comparative evidence is coming; clinicians should await the final results before changing practice.

item.title: Serum ferritin in children with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD): A systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined whether serum ferritin concentrations differ between children with ADHD and healthy controls, addressing inconsistent prior findings. It included 21 studies (4,058 ADHD cases and 4,533 controls) and followed PRISMA guidelines.
FINDINGS: The pooled mean difference in serum ferritin between children with ADHD and controls was -9.74 µg/L (95% CI: -16.50 to -2.98). Subgroup analyses showed substantial heterogeneity: larger effects were seen in African studies (-19.28), post-2016 publications (-19.43), smaller studies (<199 participants; -12.12), and studies using DSM-IV-TR criteria (-16.56). Heterogeneity (I²) was high across subgroups.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence suggests lower ferritin in ADHD, but the pooled effect is modest and highly heterogeneous across regions, time periods, and study designs. The wide confidence intervals and inconsistent subgroup patterns limit certainty. The review did not assess risk of bias or adjust for confounders (e.g., diet, comorbidities), and publication bias was not formally excluded. The clinical significance of a ~10 µg/L difference is unclear without data linking ferritin to functional outcomes.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current evidence does not justify routine ferritin screening or iron supplementation in ADHD solely based on ferritin levels. Future longitudinal studies with standardized ferritin assays and clinical endpoints are needed before considering changes to practice.

item.title: Effects of Benzodiazepines on Heart Failure Outcomes and Adverse Events: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined whether benzodiazepine (BZD) use for insomnia is associated with adverse heart failure (HF) outcomes in high-risk populations. Eleven observational studies were included, with follow-up ranging from 180 days to 15 years.
FINDINGS: Benzodiazepine use was associated with increased risks of HF incidence (HR = 1.41, 95% CI 1.16–1.72) and HF hospitalization (HR = 1.29, 95% CI 1.01–1.65) compared to non-use. It also showed higher HF hospitalization risk than antipsychotics, z-drugs, and suvorexant. All included studies were observational, limiting causal inference.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence suggests an association between BZD use and worse HF outcomes, but causality cannot be established due to the observational design. Confounding by indication (e.g., insomnia itself may worsen HF outcomes) and lack of randomized data weaken conclusions. The effect sizes are modest and may not translate to clinically meaningful differences in all patients.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Caution is warranted when prescribing BZDs to patients with or at risk of HF, but insomnia management should not be withheld without considering alternatives. Further research—particularly randomized or well-controlled studies—is needed to clarify causality and guide safer prescribing.

item.title: Efficacy of a Prescription-Based Mobile Digital Therapeutic as an Adjunct to Pharmacotherapy for the Acute Phase of Panic Disorder: Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This multicenter, single-blind RCT (n=61 completers) tested whether adding a prescription-based mobile digital therapeutic (DTx) to pharmacotherapy improves acute-phase panic disorder symptoms (frequent panic attacks) over 8 weeks. The DTx combined structured CBT modules, just-in-time panic coping, and daily tracking.
FINDINGS: The DTx group achieved a 40.29% (SD 26.68%) reduction in PDSS-SR scores versus 17.61% (SD 30.37%) in controls at week 8 (P=.007). Benefits emerged early (week 2: 26.66% vs 11.05%; P=.02). Responder rate (≥40% PDSS-SR reduction) was higher with DTx (53.12% vs 17.24%; P=.007). Adherence averaged 78.12%; no difference between responders/nonresponders.
INTERPRETATION: The trial suggests adjunctive DTx yields statistically significant and clinically detectable improvements in panic severity and related cognitions, with early onset and sustained effects. Strengths include RCT design, objective adherence metrics, and clinically meaningful responder thresholds. Limitations include small sample, single-blind design (assessors unblinded), short 8-week horizon, and lack of long-term follow-up. Funding sources and adverse events were not reported in the abstract.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: DTx could be considered as a practical adjunct to pharmacotherapy for acute-phase panic disorder, particularly where access to CBT is limited. Clinicians should monitor adherence and integrate app-generated data into routine care, while awaiting replication and longer-term outcomes.

item.title: Association between cortisol levels and psychosis in at-risk and diagnosed individuals: protocol for a systematic review.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This is a protocol for a systematic review examining whether cortisol levels (a marker of HPA-axis dysregulation) are associated with psychosis in at-risk populations and in patients with diagnosed psychotic disorders. The review will include case-control and cohort studies to clarify the temporal and cross-sectional links between cortisol and psychosis.
FINDINGS: The protocol specifies comprehensive searches across five databases plus Google Scholar, inclusion of case-control and cohort designs, and dual risk-of-bias assessment with the Joanna Briggs Institute tool and GRADE. No results are reported yet; the review is ongoing and registered in PROSPERO.
INTERPRETATION: Because this is a protocol, no empirical findings are available. The planned methodology appears rigorous, but the ultimate strength of the evidence will depend on the quality and heterogeneity of the included studies. Until results are published, clinical implications remain uncertain.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: At present, this protocol does not change practice. Clinicians should await the completed review to see whether cortisol measurement could aid risk stratification or monitoring in psychosis.

item.title: Eye Movement Desensitisation and Reprocessing (EMDR) for ICU-related psychological distress among adult intensive care survivors: a scoping review.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: Post-intensive care syndrome includes PTSD, anxiety, and depression after adult ICU admission. EMDR is a trauma-focused therapy, but its evidence in ICU survivors is emerging. This scoping review mapped the literature on EMDR for ICU-related psychological distress.
FINDINGS: Seven publications (six independent samples) were included; participants were adults with ICU-related PTSD symptoms, delirium-related disturbances, or COVID-19 distress. EMDR (standard or R-TEP) was associated with reductions in trauma-related distress; improvements in anxiety/depression were less consistent. Qualitative reports noted better integration of ICU experiences. Methodological heterogeneity, small samples, overlapping cohorts, and limited controlled data constrain conclusions.
INTERPRETATION: Confidence in the evidence is low due to design limitations and small, heterogeneous samples. No controlled trials were identified, so effectiveness remains unproven. The signal of benefit is plausible but preliminary; larger RCTs with standardised outcomes and longer follow-up are needed before EMDR can be recommended routinely in ICU survivors.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: EMDR cannot yet be considered an evidence-based treatment for ICU-related psychological distress. Clinicians may consider it cautiously in selected cases, but should prioritise established trauma-focused therapies with stronger evidence bases and monitor outcomes closely.

item.title: Communication strategies in medical imaging departments for autistic patients. A systematic review exploring person-centred care practices.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review (PROSPERO-registered, PRISMA-guided) synthesised six studies on communication interventions in medical imaging departments to improve accessibility for autistic patients, primarily in MRI and paediatric settings.
FINDINGS: Five of six studies were paediatric; three focused on MRI. Interventions included picture schedules, at-home procedural videos, and iPad social scripts. Qualitative synthesis identified three themes: flexible communication fosters acceptance, optimised communication improves experience and scan completion, and outcomes should balance patient perspectives with quantitative metrics.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is small (n=6), heterogeneous, and at high risk of bias; most studies are paediatric and MRI-focused, limiting generalisability to adults or other imaging modalities. The reported improvements in experience and completion rates are plausible but not quantified with effect sizes or confidence intervals, so clinical significance remains uncertain. The review’s strength lies in its structured synthesis and identification of research gaps rather than definitive effect estimates.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current findings support trialling flexible, multimodal communication strategies in imaging departments for autistic patients, especially children undergoing MRI, while awaiting higher-quality trials that measure both patient-reported and objective outcomes.

item.title: Treatment Trajectories of Methylphenidate versus Risperidone in Preschool ADHD: A 12-Week Retrospective Study.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The study compared 12-week trajectories of symptom change and functional outcomes between methylphenidate and risperidone monotherapies in preschool-aged boys with ADHD in a naturalistic, non-randomized retrospective chart review.
FINDINGS: Thirty-eight drug-naïve boys (52–72 months) completed 12 weeks of monotherapy (methylphenidate n=20, risperidone n=18). Two-way repeated-measures ANOVA showed no significant Time × Group interaction for core ADHD symptoms (CPRS-R:S subscales, p > 0.05), with both groups improving equally and plateauing after week 6. For broader functioning (SDQ), significant Time × Group interactions emerged (p < 0.05): methylphenidate produced earlier global behavioral improvement by week 3, whereas risperidone showed later gains in conduct problems (after week 6) and emotional symptoms (week 12).
INTERPRETATION: The study’s non-randomized, retrospective design and small, male-only sample limit causal inference and generalizability. Blinding and randomization were absent, and baseline differences were not controlled, raising confounding risk. Despite statistically significant SDQ interactions, effect sizes and clinical relevance are unclear without reported magnitudes. The parallel ADHD symptom reduction suggests no superiority for either drug on core symptoms, while functional differences may reflect distinct timelines rather than differential efficacy.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These preliminary findings do not justify choosing one agent over the other for core ADHD symptoms in preschoolers. Clinicians should await RCTs with larger, mixed-gender samples and longer follow-up before altering practice, while noting possible earlier functional gains with methylphenidate.

item.title: A Problem-Solving Therapy With Apple Watch Support for College Students With Alcohol Use Disorder Symptoms: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The study tested a novel, remote problem-solving therapy augmented by an Apple Watch (PST-APPLE) versus education-only control in college students with alcohol use disorder (AUD) symptoms. It aimed to assess feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary effectiveness on alcohol-related outcomes and drinking motives.
FINDINGS: Twenty-six students (mean age 22.5 years) were randomized 1:1. At 3 months, the intervention group showed reductions in AUDIT (mean difference −4.70, 95% CI −8.69 to −0.70) and in DMQR social (−0.85, 95% CI −1.51 to −0.18) and enhancement (−0.75, 95% CI −1.47 to −0.04) drinking motives versus control. Within-group paired t-tests also indicated reductions in AUDIT and RAPI scores post-intervention.
INTERPRETATION: This pilot RCT suggests PST-APPLE is feasible and acceptable, with small-to-moderate baseline-adjusted effects on alcohol misuse and drinking motives. However, the sample is tiny, not powered for efficacy, and lacks blinding of participants and therapists; effect sizes may be overestimated. Long-term outcomes and generalizability to broader student populations remain unknown.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current evidence is insufficient to change practice; PST-APPLE may be promising for digitally literate college students, but larger, adequately powered trials with longer follow-up are needed before recommending adoption.

item.title: Antidepressant maintenance versus active monitoring after depression remission: a decision analysis and framework linking recurrence probability and patient preferences.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This decision-analysis model compared long-term outcomes of antidepressant maintenance therapy versus active monitoring after remission from major depressive disorder (MDD), quantifying the trade-off between reduced depression recurrence and increased antidepressant exposure across patients with varying prior episode histories.
FINDINGS: Over a 5-year horizon, the model estimated that averting one month of depression required 1.5 additional years of antidepressant use in patients with 4–5 prior episodes, 2.8 years with 2–3 episodes, 5.1 years after one moderate-to-severe episode, and 11.8 years after one mild episode. The trade-off ratio increased steeply with fewer prior episodes, reflecting lower baseline recurrence risk.
INTERPRETATION: The study provides a transparent framework linking recurrence probability, treatment burden, and patient preferences, but relies on modeling assumptions rather than empirical data. The wide variation in trade-off ratios highlights the need for individualized risk–benefit assessment. The model’s validity depends on the accuracy of input parameters (e.g., recurrence rates, episode duration) and may not generalize to settings with different treatment practices or patient populations.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This model can guide shared decision-making by translating abstract relapse data into concrete trade-offs, helping clinicians and patients weigh maintenance therapy against active monitoring based on episode history and personal values. However, it should be used cautiously until validated in real-world cohorts.

item.title: Addiction management and rehabilitation programs in Saudi Arabia: a scoping review of current practices and opportunities for healthcare technology integration.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This scoping review maps current addiction management and rehabilitation programs in Saudi Arabia and explores opportunities for healthcare technology integration, addressing fragmented evidence and evolving service models in a context with strict legal and social controls.
FINDINGS: Nine studies (1995–2024) showed a shift from detoxification-focused care to multidisciplinary rehabilitation with therapeutic communities and aftercare, but long-term retention was poor, relapse and readmission were common, and community-based services were underused. Social factors like unemployment and family conflict consistently impacted outcomes. Healthcare technology use was minimal, with no studies on telehealth, mobile apps, remote monitoring, or AI-supported care. Methodological quality was moderate overall, with only three high-quality studies.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is limited and heterogeneous, with moderate methodological quality and no high-quality evaluations of digital interventions. While service evolution is evident, persistent gaps in long-term support and community integration undermine effectiveness. The absence of technology-based studies highlights a major research and implementation gap rather than proven ineffectiveness.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current practice remains largely traditional, with limited integration of digital tools despite potential benefits. Clinicians should be cautious about extrapolating benefits from other settings; more robust, locally relevant research is needed before advocating widespread adoption of healthcare technologies in Saudi addiction care.

item.title: Ketamine Use Disorder and Entrenchment of Delusional Beliefs: A Case Report.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The case report examines a 36-year-old man with ketamine use disorder (KUD) who developed persistent delusional beliefs over 2 years of heavy ketamine use, highlighting the limited evidence on treating KUD and associated psychotic symptoms.
FINDINGS: The patient met DSM-5-TR criteria for KUD with no prior psychiatric diagnoses (other than alcohol use disorder). His delusions were grandiose and hyper-religious, maintained at delusional intensity despite limited functional impact. No quantitative outcomes (e.g., symptom scales) were reported.
INTERPRETATION: This is a single case report with no comparator, making it impossible to infer causality or generalizability. The lack of standardized treatment data underscores the preliminary nature of the evidence. The clinical significance of the delusions remains unclear due to the absence of functional impairment metrics.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The case underscores the need for vigilance regarding psychotic symptoms in chronic ketamine users but does not inform treatment decisions due to its anecdotal nature. Further research is required to guide management of KUD and its psychiatric sequelae.

item.title: From discovery to proof: a Translation Evidence Map for precision psychiatry.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This Personal View proposes a Translation Evidence Map (TEM) to stage claims in precision psychiatry from discovery (Level 0) to post-deployment monitoring (Level 6), aiming to improve individual-patient decisions by quantifying clinically meaningful heterogeneity across biomarkers, data types, and analytical methods.
FINDINGS: The TEM framework evaluates claims based on measurement reliability, generalisable inference, decision value, safe delivery, and proportionality to risk/clinical need/inaction. Examples include inflammatory and circuit-based depression stratification, psychosis relapse monitoring, and suicidality monitoring. The Map does not replace existing frameworks (e.g., GRADE, biomarker qualification) but identifies the highest defensible claim and next evidence steps for compound precision claims.
INTERPRETATION: The TEM provides a structured approach to assess the maturity of precision psychiatry claims, emphasizing transparency in evidence progression and stakeholder roles. However, as a conceptual framework, it lacks empirical validation or quantitative outcomes. Its utility depends on integration with existing regulatory and clinical pathways, and its external validity remains untested in routine care.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This framework may guide clinicians in evaluating emerging precision psychiatry tools but does not yet offer actionable clinical recommendations. Clinicians should await validation studies and regulatory approvals before adopting such methods.

item.title: Subacute effects of ketamine on neural correlates of reward processing.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The study examined whether ketamine, given to healthy volunteers, alters brain reward processing five hours after infusion (subacute phase) using fMRI during a reward task. The question matters because ketamine’s antidepressant effects may involve reward circuitry, but prior work focused mainly on acute effects. This was a single-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover study in 28 healthy adults.
FINDINGS: At 5 hours post-infusion, ketamine did not significantly change brain activation during the Monetary Incentive Delay task in either region-of-interest or whole-brain analyses. Plasma ketamine and norketamine levels confirmed expected pharmacokinetics, but neither drug exposure nor subjective effects correlated robustly with neural activation. No effect sizes or p-values are reported in the abstract.
INTERPRETATION: The single-blind, crossover design and healthy volunteer sample limit internal validity; blinding may have been compromised by ketamine’s subjective effects. The absence of detectable changes could reflect true lack of subacute reward-circuit modulation or insufficient power to detect small effects. The study cannot address whether effects would appear in patients with depression or anhedonia, where reward circuitry may be more sensitive. Overall, the evidence is preliminary and does not support subacute modulation of reward processing in healthy individuals under these methods.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current findings do not justify changing practice regarding ketamine’s use for reward-related symptoms. Clinicians should note that any antidepressant benefits likely involve mechanisms beyond subacute normalization of reward-task activation in healthy brains.

item.title: Unlocking School Nurses' Capacity for Suicide Risk Screening: Implications for Multitiered System of Supports.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The study investigated how school nurses screen students for suicide risk and whether district-level suicide prevention policies influence their screening methods, self-efficacy, and referral rates. It was a national cross-sectional survey (N = 578) examining school nurses' roles in youth suicide prevention.
FINDINGS: School nurses whose roles were explicitly defined in district suicide prevention policies were more likely to use standardized screening questions. Use of standardized screening was indirectly associated with a higher number of referrals to community services, mediated by increased screening self-efficacy.
INTERPRETATION: The cross-sectional design limits causal inference; associations do not prove that policy integration improves screening or referrals. The mediation by self-efficacy suggests a plausible mechanism, but unmeasured confounders (e.g., school resources, nurse training) could influence results. The study highlights a potential policy lever but requires longitudinal or experimental validation to confirm impact.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: If confirmed, integrating school nurses into formal suicide prevention policies could enhance standardized screening and referral practices, but current evidence is preliminary and does not yet mandate practice changes.

item.title: Law Enforcement Officers and Autism Stigma: Changes Associated With Autism Training.
item.description: PURPOSE: Law enforcement officers (LEOs) frequently interact with autistic individuals, often without autism-specific training. Limited training may contribute to stigmatizing attitudes that influence these encounters. This study evaluated changes in LEOs' autism stigma toward autistic individuals following autism training. METHODS: A nonrandomized pre-post intervention design examined changes in autism stigma among 438 LEOs who attended autism training in California or Florida.

item.title: Intrinsic capacity modifies the risk of depression and anxiety through metabolomic signature.
item.description: BACKGROUND: The World Health Organization (WHO) developed an assessment for healthy aging termed intrinsic capacity (IC). However, the association between IC and depression/anxiety remains poorly understood, with limited understanding of the underlying metabolic mechanisms. METHODS: This prospective cohort study comprised 212,033 UK Biobank participants recruited between 2006 and 2010. We calculated a UK Biobank-adapted four-domain IC deficit score using seven functional status indicators across psychological, sensory, vitality, and locomotor domains.

item.title: Psilocybin use, mental health treatment utilization, and unmet treatment need among US individuals with depression.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Psilocybin use has increased in the US alongside promising therapeutic potential for depression, raising concerns that individuals may forgo conventional mental health treatment for unsupervised psilocybin use. However, no nationally representative studies have examined whether psilocybin use is associated with differential treatment utilization or perceived unmet need for mental health care among individuals with depression.

item.title: Dissociable EEG microstate signatures of cognitive and response inhibition deficits in obsessive-compulsive disorder patients.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Inhibitory control deficits represent a core cognitive feature in patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), yet their neurophysiological mechanisms remain unclear. Electroencephalogram (EEG) microstates offer a novel framework for investigating large-scale brain network dynamics in psychiatric disorders. This cross-sectional study aimed to investigate EEG microstate dynamics in OCD patients and their relationships with cognitive and response inhibition. METHODS: A total of 91 OCD patients and 76 healthy controls were recruited.

item.title: Transcriptional signatures associated with cortical similarity network changes in adolescents with major depressive disorder.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Adolescent major depressive disorder (MDD) has been associated with cortical structural abnormalities. However, whether these structural changes correlate with gene expression profiles remains unclear. Here, we investigated the cortical similarity network alterations and the associated transcriptional patterns in adolescents with MDD using a novel Morphometric Inverse Divergence (MIND) network model. METHODS: Using structural images from 174 adolescents with MDD and 82 healthy controls (HCs), we constructed individual MIND networks based on multiple morphological features.

item.title: Distinct prosocial behaviors associated with persistent symptom trajectories in psychiatric disorders.
item.description: Prosocial behavior, the tendency to act for others' benefit, is essential for mental health. Although social contexts strongly shape prosocial behavior in healthy individuals, its relevance across psychiatric disorders remains unclear. We examined whether context-dependent prosocial behaviors were associated with baseline psychiatric symptoms and longitudinal symptom trajectories.

item.title: EDIT-B consortium: an external pan-European validation of an innovative machine learning-based test for bipolar disorder diagnosis.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Differentiating bipolar disorder (BD) from major depressive disorder (MDD) during major depressive episodes remains a significant challenge. EDIT-B is an in vitro diagnostic test based on machine learning (ML) method integrating clinical metadata with adenosine-to-inosine (A-to-I) RNA editing signatures in eight genes (GAB2, IFNAR1, IL17RA, LYN, MDM2, PRKCB, PTPRC, ZNF267) to differentiate BD from MDD. OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study is to assess and confirm the diagnostic performance of EDIT-B in a new, independent, double-blind, external, multicentre European cohort.

item.title: Sleep and Drug Use: Neuroimaging Evidence for a Multidimensional Brain Framework.
item.description: Sleep plays a critical role in the initiation and maintenance of drug use, as well as recovery among individuals with substance use disorders. Sleep is a multidimensional construct, and a growing body of research has demonstrated the relative independence of various components. Specific sleep characteristics including insomnia (self-reported sleep disturbances), short sleep duration, late sleep timing and sleep irregularity have each been associated with increased risks of drug use.

item.title: Maternal immune activation influences social behavior development in a nonhuman primate model.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Women exposed to infection during pregnancy have an increased risk of giving birth to a child who will later be diagnosed with neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) characterized by changes in social development, such as autism and schizophrenia. Preclinical rodent models of maternal immune activation (MIA) have established causal links between elevated maternal cytokines and offspring social deficits indicative of human NDDs.

item.title: An examination of chronotype associations with symptoms of depression, PTSD, and sleep disturbances in US military veterans.
item.description: PURPOSE: Chronotype is associated with depression and PTSD, which are common mental health conditions among military veterans. Few studies have examined chronotype in this population, which is known to also have more severe sleep difficulties than non-veteran community-residing adults. METHODS: In the current study, self-reported sleep and mental health symptoms were examined by chronotype using data collected from US military veterans (N = 144) participating in a multi-site post-deployment health repository.

item.title: Early Exposure to a Parent's Alcohol Use Disorder as an Adverse Childhood Experience: Neurobiological and Clinical Consequences in Adulthood.
item.description: Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are a significant determinant of health across the life course and exhibit a dose-dependent relationship with the risk of mental and physical disorders in adulthood. One common yet under-recognized ACE is growing up in a family with an alcohol problem. The objective of this study was to review current data on the neurobiological mechanisms and clinical consequences of early exposure to parental alcohol use disorder, considered an ACE, along with implications for medical practice.

item.title: Dissecting immune-psychiatric links: a Mendelian randomization analysis of antibody-mediated responses and mental health disorders.
item.description: BACKGROUND: The relationship between antibody-mediated immune responses and psychiatric disorders remains incompletely understood. We characterized the relationship between antibody-mediated immune responses and 10 typical psychiatric disorders to ultimately achieve prevention or treatment. METHODS: We obtained summary data from published genome-wide association studies, including those concerning antibody-mediated immune responses and 10 psychiatric disorders.

item.title: "They call me a glue kid, but I don't like it": Experiences of glue use among street-connected adolescents in Merauke Regency, Indonesia.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Glue-sniffing among street-connected children and adolescents is a neglected public health and social issue with acute toxicity, entrenched stigma, and long-term life-course harms. In Merauke (South Papua), everyday practices, peer dynamics, and social labeling remain under-described. OBJECTIVE: To explore lived experiences of street-connected children and adolescents who use inhalants in Merauke, focusing on initiation, accessibility, peer processes, harms, return to glue use, and perceived stigma.

item.title: AA in Brain-Memory, Dementia, Depression, Anxiety, Alzheimer's Disease, Affective and Psychiatric Disorders, and Coronary Heart Disease (CHD).
item.description: The human brain is rich in AA and DHA, which are crucial for normal brain growth and development and memory. They form a major structural component of neurons of the cerebral cortex and photoreceptor cells in the retina. AA and DHA support synaptic plasticity and contribute to efficient neurotransmission. Adequate amounts of AA and DHA support neuronal growth and the formation of new synapses and thus are crucial for memory and cognitive function.Depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, and other neurological diseases occur more frequently in those with coronary heart disease (CHD) and vice versa.

item.title: Responsiveness and minimal important change of Turkish pain-related psychological measures in chronic non-specific low back pain.
item.description: BACKGROUND: The longitudinal interpretability of Turkish pain-related psychological measures in chronic non-specific low back pain (NSLBP) remains uncertain. This study evaluated the responsiveness and minimal important change (MIC) of the Turkish Fear-Avoidance Beliefs Questionnaire (FABQ), Tampa Scale of Kinesiophobia (TSK) and Pain Catastrophizing Scale (PCS). METHODS: In this prospective, single-arm measurement-property study, 110 adults with chronic NSLBP completed baseline and 4-week assessments during a standardized rehabilitation program.

item.title: Electronic Health Record-Based Phenotyping for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: Algorithm Development and Multicenter Validation Study.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is a common psychiatric disorder, with two-thirds of affected individuals reporting severe impairment. Despite its substantial burden and moderate heritability, the etiology of OCD remains poorly understood, and treatments are often suboptimal. Although recent genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified some risk loci, much of the genetic architecture of OCD remains undiscovered, underscoring the need for scalable approaches to identify large, well-defined patient cohorts.

item.title: Flying under the radar: a qualitative examination of self-diagnosed ADHD and identity formation in young women.
item.description: BACKGROUND: In recent years, the prevalence of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) diagnoses has increased sharply, in many western countries, including Sweden, especially among women and adults. Concurrently, more people seem to identify with ADHD without having a formal diagnosis, a phenomenon that has been highlighted in the media but not examined thoroughly in research. As women with ADHD are diagnosed later in life compared to men, self-diagnosis in young women may be an important piece of puzzle to understand diagnostic processes and identification.

item.title: 'Navigating the ride': stakeholder perspectives on public transportation challenges for children with autism in India.
item.description: OBJECTIVE: To explore the perspectives of primary caregivers, healthcare professionals and transport personnel regarding the challenges associated with public transportation for children with autism spectrum disorder in India. DESIGN: This study applied a descriptive phenomenological qualitative design. SETTING: The study was conducted at a tertiary care teaching centre in South India.

item.title: Understanding participation and quality of life of university students with probable DCD using structural equation modeling.
item.description: BACKGROUNDS: Individuals with developmental coordination disorder (DCD) attending higher-education institutions face challenges in their everyday life. Nevertheless, research regarding participation and quality of life (QoL) in this population is limited. AIM: To explore determinants of participation and QoL in university students with probable DCD (pDCD) through structural equation modelling (SEM). METHODS: A cross-sectional comparative and correlational design.

item.title: Developmental and environmental differences in infants with family history of autism and ADHD during the first year of life in Brazil.
item.description: Infants with family history (FH) of autism or attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) are likely to experience a range of differences in their early development compared to infants without FH. However, the vast majority of evidence concerning the early development of these infants has come from high-income-country (HIC) contexts and has not considered the role of psychosocial environmental factors.

item.title: The ACE of Hearts Serious Game for Young People With Adverse Childhood Experiences: Experience-Based Co-Design and Agile Development Study.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Young people exposed to adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are at risk of poor mental and physical health across the life course, yet many struggle to access timely help. Serious games offer an engaging, scalable, and stigma-reducing support, but few are co-designed with young people who have lived experience of ACEs, and methodological accounts of how participatory design is operationalized alongside software delivery are scarce.

item.title: Associations Between Pain Severity and Opioid Agonist Treatment Among People With Drug Injection Experience in Australia.
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Pain is highly prevalent among people with opioid use disorder (OUD), yet it is often undertreated. Whether opioid agonist treatment (OAT) improves pain outcomes is unknown among this target population. This research aimed to explore associations between pain severity and current OAT status in a longitudinal cohort of people who inject drugs. METHODS: Data were drawn from the Melbourne Injecting Drug User Cohort Study (SuperMIX), comprising individuals with a drug injection history recruited from areas across Greater Melbourne and Geelong, Australia, between 2008 and 2024.

item.title: Criminal Legal Referrals Were Associated With Delayed Substance Use Treatment, Disparity By Housing Status.
item.description: Timely access to substance use disorder (SUD) treatment is critical to improving health outcomes, yet treatment delays remain a barrier. Using national Treatment Episode Data Set-Admissions data from the period 2017-22, we conducted the first national study to examine the association of referral pathways and housing status with treatment delays among 962,702 first-time SUD admissions. Compared with individual referrals, criminal legal referrals were associated with more than twice the odds of delayed admission.

item.title: Intranasal Delivery of Proenkephalin-Expressing Differentiated Mesenchymal Stem Cells Attenuates Morphine Dependence Behaviors and Modulates Neurotrophic Factors in Rats.
item.description: Substance use disorder is a chronic relapsing condition characterized by persistent drug seeking, cognitive impairment, and neurobiological alterations in brain reward and memory circuits. Emerging evidence suggests that dysfunction of the endogenous opioid system and reduced neurotrophic signaling contribute to the pathophysiology of opioid dependence. Cell based therapeutic strategies may provide a novel approach to modulate these neural pathways. In the present experimental study, morphine dependence was induced in adult male rats using an escalating dose regimen.

item.title: Association between plain-water consumption and suicide attempts among U.S. adolescents: Evidence from the 2017-2021 Youth Risk Behavior Survey.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Adolescent suicide attempts remain difficult to predict, in part because research has concentrated on a narrow set of risk factors. We examined whether self-reported plain-water consumption is associated with past-year suicide attempt among U.S. adolescents, whether that association is graded across levels of intake, and whether a zero-intake response adds information beyond established risk factors. METHODS: We analyzed the 2017, 2019 and 2021 cycles of the U.S. national Youth Risk Behavior Survey (n = 36,779).

item.title: The Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill in the United Kingdom and Patient and Clinician Attitudes on Legalization of Assisted Dying.
item.description: BACKGROUND: The legalization of assisted dying remains open for debate in the United Kingdom, where the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill is currently under review. It is paramount to consider patient and clinician attitudes on assisted dying and understand how legalization of assisted dying may alter care delivery in the United Kingdom.

item.title: Experiences of mothers with borderline personality disorder following an intervention to support mother-infant relationships: "more tools in my toolbox".
item.description: Motherhood is inherently demanding, and some of these demands may be amplified for women with borderline personality disorder (BPD). The exacerbation of BPD symptoms from parenting-related stressors can have adverse impacts on mother-infant relationships and infant development. This qualitative study explores Australian mothers' views of the impacts of mother-infant dialectical therapy plus (MI-DBT+).

item.title: Professional Training by Perinatal Psychiatry Access Programs: Multi-Method Approach to Characterize the State of the US Access Programs.
item.description: OBJECTIVE: Perinatal mental health (PMH) conditions often go unrecognized, undiagnosed, and untreated. Perinatal Psychiatry Access Programs (Access Programs) provide consultation, resources, and referrals to support frontline perinatal care clinicians in addressing PMH conditions. Most Access Programs also offer professional training for perinatal care clinicians. This article describes the goals of and approaches to professional training among 14 Access Programs.

item.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis: the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy and eye movement desensitization and reprocessing in children and adolescents.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis compared the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and eye movement desensitization and reprocessing (EMDR) for reducing PTSD symptoms in children and adolescents (6–18 years) exposed to traumatic events, using randomized controlled trials (RCTs).
FINDINGS: Five RCTs (n=248) were included. No significant difference was found between CBT and EMDR for child-reported PTSD symptoms (SMD 0.18; 95% CI -0.07 to 0.43; I²=0%) or parent-reported PTSD symptoms (SMD 0.23; 95% CI -0.02 to 0.48; I²=0%). Anxiety outcomes were not statistically significant (SMD 0.44; 95% CI -0.19 to 1.07; I²=69%). Depression symptoms were higher in the CBT group than in the EMDR group (SMD 0.44; 95% CI 0.13 to 0.76; I²=0%).
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is small (five trials, 248 participants) and shows no clear superiority of one therapy over the other for PTSD or anxiety. The statistically significant difference in depression favoring EMDR is based on a single pooled estimate with wide CIs and no clinical context for what constitutes a meaningful change. Heterogeneity was low for most outcomes, but the anxiety result showed substantial inconsistency (I²=69%). Overall, the certainty of evidence is low due to the small number of trials and potential risk of bias.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current evidence does not support choosing CBT over EMDR or vice versa for PTSD in children and adolescents based solely on efficacy. Clinicians should continue to select therapy based on patient preference, availability, and clinician expertise until more robust data emerge.

item.title: EVIDENCE-BASED PHARMACOTHERAPY FOR ANXIETY DISORDERS COMORBID WITH PTSD: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review with GRADE assessment evaluated pharmacological treatments for anxiety symptoms in adults with PTSD, including those with comorbid anxiety disorders or clinically significant anxiety, synthesizing RCTs and prospective cohorts from 2000–2025.
FINDINGS: Across 22 studies (n=2,708), SSRIs reduced anxiety symptoms (SMD −0.46, 95% CI −0.62 to −0.30; moderate certainty) and PTSD symptoms (SMD −0.43, 95% CI −0.58 to −0.28; moderate certainty). SNRIs reduced anxiety symptoms (SMD −0.38, 95% CI −0.55 to −0.21; low certainty), while atypical antipsychotics showed possible benefit but increased discontinuation due to adverse events (RR 2.14, 95% CI 1.43–3.21).
INTERPRETATION: The evidence supports SSRIs for reducing anxiety in PTSD with moderate certainty, though diagnostic clarity for comorbid anxiety disorders is limited. SNRIs offer lower-certainty benefits, and atypical antipsychotics carry a higher risk of adverse effects. The review’s strength lies in its systematic approach and GRADE assessment, but heterogeneity in diagnostic criteria and study designs weakens generalisability to routine care.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: SSRIs remain a reasonable first-line option for anxiety symptoms in PTSD, but clinicians should carefully assess for comorbid anxiety disorders and monitor tolerability. SNRIs and atypical antipsychotics should be used cautiously given lower certainty and higher adverse event rates.

item.title: Home-Based Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation for Depression: From Feasibility to Clinical Implementation.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This narrative review examines the clinical implementation of home-based transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) for major depressive disorder (MDD), synthesizing evidence on efficacy, adherence, safety, and real-world feasibility following FDA premarket approval of the Flow FL-100 device in 2025.
FINDINGS: Randomized controlled trials indicate that home-based tDCS is effective when delivered with adequate cumulative dosing, structured protocols, and supervision or adherence monitoring; shorter or unsupervised protocols show less favorable outcomes. High adherence (reported across >30,000 supervised sessions) is supported by user-centered device design, standardized training, remote monitoring, and scalable supervision models. No skin lesions or serious adverse events attributable to tDCS were reported in a large academic clinical program.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is primarily derived from RCTs and large clinical programs, suggesting that home-based tDCS can be safely and effectively implemented under structured conditions. However, as a narrative review, it lacks systematic synthesis and may overstate generalizability. Key uncertainties remain regarding the independent contributions of dose, duration, and supervision, as well as the optimal integration into routine care. The lack of blinding in many real-world protocols and potential selection bias in adherence data limit internal validity.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Home-based tDCS may soon be a viable option for MDD in interventional psychiatry settings, provided strict protocols, supervision, and monitoring are in place. Clinicians should await clearer dosing guidelines and patient selection criteria before widespread adoption, and remain vigilant for subtle safety signals in unsupervised use.

item.title: A Phase 3, Multicenter, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Trial Evaluating the Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of Serdexmethylphenidate/d-Methylphenidate Capsules in Chinese Children with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of serdexmethylphenidate/dexmethylphenidate (SDX/d-MPH) capsules in Chinese children aged 6–12 years with ADHD, addressing whether this novel methylphenidate formulation provides symptom control superior to placebo over 3–4 weeks.
FINDINGS: 55 children were randomized (SDX/d-MPH n=28; placebo n=27). At week 3, SDX/d-MPH showed a greater reduction in ADHD-RS-5 total score versus placebo (LSM change difference −5.8 [SE 2.58], p=0.0292; effect size 0.61). At week 4, significant improvements were seen in ADHD-RS-5 total (−8.4 [2.69]), inattention (−4.4 [1.69]), hyperactivity-impulsivity (−3.7 [1.27]), CGI-S (−0.8 [0.28]), CGI-I (0.9 [0.27]), and WREMB-R total (−3.7 [1.35]) and evening (−3.2 [1.03]) scores. Most adverse events were mild to moderate; no new safety signals emerged.
INTERPRETATION: The study demonstrates statistically significant superiority of SDX/d-MPH over placebo on core ADHD symptoms with a moderate effect size, but the small sample (n=55) and short 4-week duration limit confidence in durability and generalizability. The trial was double-blind and placebo-controlled, strengthening internal validity, though the narrow population (Chinese children 6–12 years) and lack of active comparator constrain external validity. The effect size (0.61) suggests a clinically modest but potentially meaningful improvement for some patients.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: SDX/d-MPH may offer an additional stimulant option for Chinese children with ADHD, but given the small sample and short follow-up, clinicians should weigh benefits against limited long-term safety and efficacy data; current first-line treatments remain appropriate until larger, longer trials confirm durability and comparative effectiveness.

item.title: ADVANCES IN RESEARCH OF PSYCHOTHERAPY FOR SOCIAL ANXIETY DISORDER.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This narrative review synthesizes recent research on psychological interventions for Social Anxiety Disorder (SAD), focusing on efficacy, mechanisms, and delivery formats. It covers established treatments like CBT and newer approaches (mindfulness, ACT, VRET) to guide clinical decision-making.
FINDINGS: The review highlights strong empirical support for CBT in SAD, while evidence for mindfulness-based interventions, ACT, and VRET is mixed and requires further study. Digital technologies (e.g., online CBT) are increasingly used as delivery tools rather than standalone treatments. Key gaps include limited understanding of active treatment components and long-term functional outcomes.
INTERPRETATION: As a narrative review, this study lacks the rigor of a systematic review or meta-analysis, making it prone to selection bias and unsystematic synthesis. The conclusions align with established evidence (CBT efficacy) but downplay heterogeneity in newer interventions. The focus on mechanisms and patient-treatment matching is valuable but lacks concrete data or actionable insights.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: CBT remains the gold standard for SAD, while other modalities (e.g., ACT, VRET) may be considered adjunctively but require individualized assessment. Clinicians should prioritize evidence-based therapies and monitor long-term functional gains, acknowledging the preliminary nature of newer approaches.
